scope_note: Four bounded syntheses are retained after direct-record search: one deterministic conversion of Meta's rounded 2024 Henrico water-withdrawal observation and three governed, descriptive county comparison gaps. No construction, operating, supplier, household, tax-receipt, incentive-cost, or public-service-cost model is added because the public record lacks the needed project-specific bases and arbitrary allocation shares would create false precision. Every retained estimate is visibly modeled, unallocated to the selected building, non-additive, and noncausal.

estimates.label: Unit-converted annual water withdrawal

interval.interpretation: The band reflects rounding of the source's displayed 92 megaliters to the nearest whole megaliter before conversion; it is not a confidence interval.

provenance.detail: Exact unit-conversion factor used for presentation

estimates.confidence_rationale: The facility row and conversion are reproducible, but the published amount is rounded and its site-level measurement basis is not specified.
estimates.decision_relevance: Preserves the public facility-level water observation in a compatible presentation unit while the shared canonical direct-evidence metric is absent.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Canonical annual water-withdrawal metric, unrounded meter data, withdrawal source allocation, consumption, reuse, discharge, and billing by facility

derivation.formula: reported Henrico water withdrawal in megaliters × 264,172.052 gallons per megaliter
assumptions: The displayed source value is rounded to the nearest whole megaliter.
The estimate must not be presented as observed, audited, source-reported, or causal.

limitations: The source rounds to whole megaliters and permits meter, utility, design-estimate, or proxy inputs where applicable.
Withdrawal is not consumption; no site-specific consumption or discharge value is reported.
The value is not an audited municipal billing record and is not allocated to the selected building.
estimates.notes: Source-reported facility value carried as a visibly modeled unit conversion because no compatible canonical direct-evidence metric exists.

estimates.label: Modeled county real GDP comparison gap

period.label: 2024 host-county outcome relative to a mechanically matched benchmark; campus opening year 2020

scope.label: Meta Henrico campus and Henrico County

interval.interpretation: The envelope is the larger of plus or minus 5 percentage points or twice the 2012-2019 pre-period RMSE. It is a fit sensitivity, not a statistical confidence interval.

parameters.name: comparison_2024_value

provenance.detail: Inverse-distance weighted 2024 value from 20 comparison counties

parameters.transformation: Subtracted from host and used as denominator

parameters.name: pre_period_rmse_percent
parameters.transformation: Sets fit-sensitivity width subject to 5-point floor

estimates.confidence_rationale: The calculation is reproducible, but concurrent county activity and treatment timing prevent attribution.
estimates.decision_relevance: Shows Henrico County's 2024 divergence from a reproducible comparison benchmark without assigning the divergence to Meta.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: A causal design with complete county exposure history, treatment isolation, pre-trend diagnostics, placebos, spillover rules, and robustness checks

assumptions: Matching uses 2012-2019 log level, average log growth, and growth volatility.
All selected-study counties are excluded from the donor pool.
The 2020 campus opening is not assumed to be first county exposure or an isolated treatment date.

limitations: This comparison is descriptive and must not be interpreted as a data-center effect.
Opening timing does not isolate construction, later expansions, or concurrent investments.
The donor screen cannot exclude every unobserved treatment.
The interval is fit sensitivity, not statistical confidence.
estimates.notes: Descriptive benchmark gap only; no causal_design metadata is attached.
